title: WPSB/467/2014 of Neeraj Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 467 of 2014
Neeraj Kumar. ..... Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. ..... Respondents.
Mr. Krishan Mohan Agarwal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent no.1
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for respondent nos. 4 & 5.
Dated: July 02, 2015
Coram :Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral):
 The petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following reliefs:
"1. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari to vanish the corruption
and the corrupt practice of illegal promotion
of the respondent nos. 4 & 5 made by the
respondent no. 1 to 3 in violation to the
Service Regulation 2004 UREDA, declaring
their present posting illegal, null and void.
2. Issue a writ or order in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent nos. 1 to
3 to consider the petitioner's promotion and
transfer for the administration of equity and
justice."
2. The petitioner was appointed in the year 1987 as
Junior Engineer in Non-Conventional Energy
Development Agency (hereinafter referred to as NEDA),
when the State of U.P. was not yet divided into State of
Uttar Pradesh and State of Uttarakhand. The petitioner
was promoted as Project Officer on 16.10.1995.
Respondent no.4, on the other hand, was appointed in
NEDA as Project Officer on 08.05.1984. The 5th
respondent was appointed as Project Officer in NEDA on
03.05.1984. The petitioner has approached this Court

2
with the reliefs, which we have already quoted. Pleadings
have already been exchanged.
3. We heard Mr. Krishan Mohan Agarwal, learned
counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner, Mr. Ramji
Srivastava, learned counsel for respondent nos. 2 & 3, Mr.
Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for respondent nos. 4 & 5
as well as Mr. Pradeep Joshi, learned Govt. Pleader.
4. By order dated 20.10.2004, respondent 4 & 5 were
promoted as Deputy Chief Project Officers. This was done
after the Selection Committee made recommendations.
Still later, in the year 2006, the 4th respondent was further
promoted as Chief Project Officer by order dated
04.05.2006.
5. Sri Krishan Mohan Agarwal, learned counsel for the
petitioner would submit that this is a case involving
fraud/ corruption as the respondent nos. 4 & 5 were not
qualified to be appointed. It is submitted that respondent
no. 4 & 5 have misrepresented that they were Senior
Project Officers and, on the basis of the same, the
promotion was effected to the post of Deputy Chief
Project Officer. It is submitted that under the Regulations
made, to be qualified to be promoted as the Deputy Chief
Project Officer, the person should have 20 years' total
service and also four years' service in UREDA; respondent
nos. 4 & 5 are not in possession of the same. It is further
submitted that in the matter of further promotion, to the
post of Chief Project Officer, granted to the 4th
respondent, even after the relaxation granted under the
Rules, the 4th respondent was actually not eligible and it is
submitted, therefore, that the promotion orders are
infirm. It is submitted that respondent nos. 4 & 5 have not
worked, for a single day, as Senior Project Officers. In
fact, support was sought to be drawn from the response to

3
the query made under the Right to Information Act given
by UREDA, wherein it is stated that respondent nos. 4 & 5
have not been promoted as Senior Project Officers. It is
submitted that this is being a case, where there is fraud,
corruption and clear violation of regulations, the Court
should interfere in the matter, even if there is delay. In the
matter of delay, it is submitted that the petitioner was
representing the matter. Representations did not evoke
any response and the petitioner made applications under
the Right to Information Act, and after receiving
information, petitioner has approached this Court.
6. It is also brought to our notice that respondent nos.
4 & 5 were involved in serious financial irregularities. In
this connection, attention is made to the document
annexed to the rejoinder, which would show that without
work being done, a contractor was enable to get
mobilization advance, and reliance was placed on a fake
bank guarantee.
7. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel appearing on
behalf of respondent nos. 2 & 3 would point out that the
writ petition actually appears to be in the nature of a
public interest petition. He points out that perusal of
prayers would show that no order was specifically
challenged. In regard to the second prayer, he would
submit that, actually, the petitioner had filed a writ
petition seeking to challenge the transfer and that was
dismissed.
8. He would submit that the petitioner does not have
any locus-standi. He points out that petitioner was
appointed as a Junior Engineer in the year 1987 and he
became Project Officer only in the year 1995, whereas;
respondent nos. 4 & 5 became Project Officers in the year
1984 and they are good 11 years senior to the petitioner.

4
He points out that respondent nos. 4 & 5 were actually
promoted as Senior Project Officers on 20.08.1988 and
18.07.1989. He also submits that the seniority list of
Project Officers was prepared, in which the petitioner was
shown below respondent nos. 4 & 5 and that was not
challenged.
9. Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel appearing on
behalf of respondent nos. 4 & 5 would submit that writ
petition deserves to be dismissed, firstly on the ground
that there is clear laches. In other words, he would submit
that the orders were passed at considerable distance of
time and the writ petitioner has not approached the
Court, except with laches. It is further submitted that the
petitioner has an alternative remedy. He refers to Section
4 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Tribunal Act. He
would point out that the prayers in the writ petition are
vague. He would refer us to order dated 11.06.1996 to
contend that the respondents were indeed promoted as
Senior Project Officer. He would also submit that the post
of Senior Project Officer falls in Group-A. He would deny
the allegations that the promotions were illegal. He would
submit that respondent nos. 4 & 5 were promoted, after
giving relaxation by the Selection Committee.
10. Petitioner has a case, that perusal of the Office
Order would show that the petitioner was working as
Project Officer, and it is also the case of the petitioner that
there was only one post of Senior Project Officer. And it is
his case that there is no post of Senior Project Officer in
NEDA and the person posted was sent back. In regard to
the said order, the case of Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned
counsel for respondent nos. 2 & 3 is that the said order
refers to the officers with reference of the original posting
as Project Officer.

5
11. We have already noticed the prayers. No doubt, the
petitioner has referred to illegalities as he sees it in regard
to promotions to both the posts of Chief Project Officer
and Deputy Chief Project Officer. When it comes to the
prayers, no order, as such, is produced and there is no
specific reference to any order in the prayer portion. We
are more concerned about the aspect of laches in this case.
Admittedly, the promotion of respondent nos. 4 & 5 to the
post of Deputy Chief Project Officers took place on
20.10.2004. The writ petition is filed in the year 2014, i.e.
after ten years. The only answer given by the learned
counsel for the petitioner would appear to be that the
petitioner has been making representations and did not
evoke any response. It is settled law that the cause of
action arises the ticking of the clock cannot be explained
away by merely alleging that the petitioner was
representing the matter. It is incumbent upon the writ
applicant to come to the Court within a reasonable time
and the question of laches is to be decided with reference
to the context of the case. In this case, the question of
laches is infact, a matter which must be decided with
reference to the effect of delay on the rights of others. This
is a case, where the petitioner, while he claims in the
second prayer promotion for himself, has emphasized
more the illegality of the promotions of respondent no.4.
In other words, the relief, which he has emphasized, is a
relief, which has an impact on the rights of others. In such
circumstances, the issue of laches must be examined with
effect of rights of others, namely respondent nos. 4 & 5. A
perusal of paragraph nos. 12 and 13 of the writ petition,
reveals the following pleadings:-
"12. That the petitioner came to know about
this bungling, manipulation,
misrepresentation and malafidies in

6
promotion by play of fraud which has affected
the promotion and transfer of the petitioner
and other similarly situated Senior Officers of
UREDA. The rampant corruption and fraud
has played a vital role in the escape of the
transparency and clean public life of the
public servants. The petitioner under RTI
2005 sought record of the DPC about the
administrative direct link official with the
chairman briefed for the promotion on the
post for which the respondent nos. 4 & 5 were
illegally promoted against the fair play and
transparency in the working of the office to
which respondent nos. 4 & 5 by colourful
exercise of power due to fraud, become the top
officials superseding the claim of the collogues
and flouting the law, cause also losses to the
public exchequer and malign the goodwill not
only of the public servant but also of the
Government of Uttarakhand. The query raised
in the RTI reply on 25.04.2014 had been
escaped hence departmental appeal was filed
but that too was rejected so the second appeal
before the Hon'ble RTI Commission,
Dehradun was filed, and a reminder thereto
was given on 01.12.2014, the second appeal is
pending to the knowledge of the petitioner
before the RTI Commission. The true copy of
RTI query concealed dated 25.04.2014, appeal
and reminder memo of 2nd appeal dated
09.07.2014, dated 01.12.2014 to the RTI
Commission; is collectively being filed
herewith as annexure no.10 to this writ
petition.
13. That the petitioner in the mean time
thought it fit to give a notice to the respondent
nos. 1 & 2 including the Director UREDA to
represent their stand on the fraud played by
the respondent nos. 4 & 5 in overriding. The
mandatory requirement of promotion. The
respondent no.4 (Mr. Arun Kumar Tyagi)
neither served/worked as Senior Project
Officer Group A/Class-I (one year for Deputy
Chief Project Officer) nor fulfill the
requirement of 20 years (the chairman
UREDA without jurisdiction dispensed
with/exempted 3 years 2 months period as
Class I inspite of this illegal exemption the
respondent no.4 was not having working

7
experience in Class I for the period of 15 years
4 months) working experience of Class I/
Group A service for the post of Chief Project
Officer, depicted in Service Regulation 2004
UREDA at appendix 'A' true copy whereof
already annexed in former collective annexure
no.9. The true copy of notice dated 05.12.2014
sent through Mr. Krishan Mohan Agarwal
Advocate to the respondent nos. 1 & 2
including the Director UREDA is being
annexed herewith as annexure no. 11 to this
writ petition."
12. That is to say, after making vague allegations, the
petitioner does not specifically say as to when he came to
know about the alleged bungling, manipulation and
misrepresentation. The petitioner also relies on the
service entries to point out that there is no promotion as
Senior Project Officer.
13. Normally, we cannot assume that when promotions
were made in the department, the petitioner would not
know about it. Petitioner does not have a case that the
petitioner came to know about it only on a later point of
time. Therefore, if we go by the normal presumption
about knowledge of the orders, as it would have happened
in the normal course of events, which every Court is
entitled to presume, there is gross and inordinate delay in
the matter of the petitioner approaching the Court and
challenging the order passed on 20.10.2004. If the
petitioner is to be told off the gates, by reason of the
inordinate delay in the matter of challenging the order
dated 20.10.2004, then its challenge to the order dated
04.05.2006 may not be countenanced. In this context, it
is immediately necessary to remind ourselves, that the
petitioner was appointed in the year 1987 as a Junior
Engineer, was granted promotion as Project Officer only
in the year 1995 as against respondent nos. 4 & 5, who
were promoted in the year 1984. To a pointed question,

8
the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
the petitioner could not have aspired for being promoted
as Deputy Chief Project Officer in the year 2004.
Therefore, in that sense his locus, with regard to the
promotion, itself, becomes suspect. That apart, there is no
explanation for delay in challenging the promotion of the
4th respondent to the further higher post of Chief Project
Officer. An attempt was made by the petitioner to
persuade us to still entertaining the writ petition on the
basis of principles laid down by the Apex Court in the
context of fraud. In the first place, we are not too sure,
whether the petitioner has established the case of fraud at
all. In the year 1996, in UREDA, the respondent nos. 4 & 5
were given an up-gradation to the post of Senior Project
Officers, Grade-II. So it is not as if that the claim that was
no promotion for which support is drawn from the
response to the query under the Right to Information Act,
can be said to be made out. As we have already noted, the
petitioner was not qualified for being promoted as Deputy
Chief Project Officer or, of course, as Chief Project Officer
in the year 2004 or 2006 respectively. Respondents have
a case that after giving the necessary relaxation they
became eligible in terms of the Rules. The matter was
considered by the Selection Committee. The petitioner
slept over his rights and did not move the Court, despite
his own case that he has been moving the representations.
14. The petitioner refers to acts of corruption. We do
not think, we should be persuaded to entertain such a plea
to consider a case, where the petitioner himself comes
late, and the grounds are as he has taken. We do not think
that the petitioner, in the circumstances, has made out a
case for exercise of discretionary jurisdiction under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India. In the

9
circumstances, we would think that we need not grant the
reliefs sought in this case.
15. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that he may be permitted to represent the matter before
Competent Authority. We would not think that in this
case, at this length of time, we should permit the
petitioner to represent the matter and revive the
controversy, which we have already held that this is a
matter where the petitioner has approached this Court
late. Accordingly, we do not accept this contention. The
writ petition fails and is dismissed as such. No order as to
costs.
(V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 02.07.2015
